title: Void Ending in a Sextile to Pluto
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The sextile is one of the two friendly aspects. Picatrix ties the Moon to the fortunes by trine and sextile whenever a work is meant to prosper, and grades the sextile as the aspect of moderate friendship: the signs it joins are kin in action but not in passion, so the concord between them is a lukewarm one.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a sextile to Pluto, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his buried endings. Pluto is unknown to Picatrix, found in 1930 and outside the world the book describes at every point. Any reading of it here is this almanac's extension of Picatrix's doctrine, never the source's own words. Named for the Roman lord of the underworld, it is read as the far, dark hinge of the set: a course that closes on it ends in the buried kind of ending, the small death of a matter before the next sign begins.
